# Subject: Behavioral breaks outside static evidence

The declaration, the symbol, the layout and the imports are all unchanged, yet an unchanged old consumer breaks at runtime because the implementation's behavior changed. The correct static verdict is NO_CHANGE for the declared interface; the break is recorded separately as behavioral_break with a runtime witness.

_4 case(s)._ [← back to all subjects](index.md)

## The pattern

Every case in this subject is a NO_CHANGE detection control with a failing runtime witness. Source and binary compatibility ask a shape question -- does the old code still compile, link and agree on layout -- and for these releases the answer is yes at every evidence depth: binary exports, DWARF, the public header AST, build data (compile_commands.json) and even the source tree all show the same declarations. What changed is the behavior behind the declaration: an error that used to be a documented return value is now an exception (case230), a returned number changed its unit (case231), a raw pointer's ownership moved from the caller to the library (case232), or an optimised definition now assumes the arguments never alias (case208). Each of those contracts lives in documentation and in the consumer's head, not in any artifact a deterministic comparison reads, so abicheck correctly reports nothing -- and NO_CHANGE here never means 'safe to ship'. ground_truth.json records the break as behavioral_break: true with truth_scope: declared-interface, and the per-case README shows the consumer that breaks. Behavioral compatibility is verified by running consumers: the library's own tests, consumer test suites, and contract tests (see docs/learn/behavioral-compatibility.md).
